notes: Promoted as the four hand-written members (two helpers, Render, Behavior) into src/actors/daObjKurumajiku_c.cpp: reverse-ROM source order, `// @symbol` on each. The destructor pair is excluded from the licensed range (see destructor grid note) and stays in its legacy one-function shards, exactly the landed daObjKuruma_c shape immediately below.

func_ov002_020b6a80 keeps its legacy `char *` parameter (agreeing with include/decl_common.h:1312, which also declares it that way); Behavior casts at the call. A typed-pointer reconciliation was tried and reverted -- the shared header is the tree's spelling and the cast is byte-free, so the TU follows it.

DESTRUCTOR GRID -- cartridge has D0 (0x020b69e4, 0x58) BELOW D1 (0x020b6a3c, 0x44); every form with a visible body emits D1,D0 (inline in-class, inline out-of-class in header, declaration-last, eight explicit-odr-use arrangements, implicit dtor, forced D1-first odr-use -- all D1,D0 per tools/tu_order_check.py). Out-of-line emits D2,D0,D1 but removes the header body the promoted descendants ov043/daObjKm1_Kurumajiku_c and ov047/daObjKm3_Kurumajiku_c inline (their D1/D0 go wrong without it). The `#pragma defer_codegen off` + forcing-object form passes but violates notes/tu-promotion-conventions.md. So the pair stays in legacy shards (one function per object, where emission order is vacuous); the vtable homes here via Behavior, its D1/D0 slots resolve to the legacy objects at link, and this object's own copies are deadstrip-discarded with the vtable (cartridge copy from the data gap).
